Allocate a split parent's displaced land to the child reach nearest each part

Source: R/reconcile_divides.R
dot-allocate_parent_parts.Rd

When a reference catchment is split among the fragments of a split reach, the D8 partition can return sub-polygons that sit nowhere near the fragment they were assigned to. The land itself is correct, it is the parent catchment and no area is missing, but the assignment of land to fragment is not.

This resolves the assignment the way the partition is itself trying to: every polygon part of the displaced land goes to the fragment whose own flowline is nearest it. Fragments whose partition already meets their flowline keep what they hold and may gain parts, so only displaced land moves, the parent's area is conserved exactly, and no two fragments can claim the same ground.

The alternatives it replaces were both spatially arbitrary: handing the whole parent to whichever fragment had the longest flowline, and handing every displaced fragment the same leftover polygon.

A fragment with no flowline cannot receive land, since there is nothing to measure against; a group in which no fragment has one is left untouched.

Usage

.allocate_parent_parts(geoms, lines, disjoint, crs)

Arguments

geoms

List of sfg, the current partition polygon of each fragment.

lines

List of sfc or NULL, each fragment's member flowlines.

disjoint

Logical marking fragments whose polygon does not meet their own flowline.

crs

CRS shared by geoms and lines.

Value

A list of sfg the same length as geoms, or NULL when there is nothing to reallocate.
